items.statement: When an antidepressant dulls MDMA's effects, there is also less MDMA in your blood.
items.why: In small trials, two antidepressants lowered how strongly people rated MDMA's effects, yet the MDMA peak in their blood was about 15 to 18 percent higher. That's second-hand, from single trials of 16 healthy people each.
items.old_statement: If an antidepressant mutes MDMA's effects, that means less MDMA is in your blood.

items.statement: In published cases of people who kept vomiting while using cannabis regularly, most found hot baths or showers helped for a while.
items.why: Most of the 211 people in published cases found this. But many people with other kinds of repeated vomiting use hot showers too.
items.old_statement: In published cases of repeated vomiting with regular cannabis use, most people found hot baths or showers eased it for a while.

items.statement: Regular cannabis use can come with repeated vomiting. In published cases, most found hot showers or baths eased it for a while.
items.why: Most of the 211 people in published cases found this. But many people with other kinds of repeated vomiting use hot showers too.

items.statement: In lab driving tests, people did just as well soon after THC, cannabis's main active part, as after a dummy version.
items.why: In 80 pooled lab studies, people weaved more in their lane and reacted more slowly than after a dummy.
items.old_statement: Soon after THC, the main active part of cannabis, people did just as well on lab driving tests as after a dummy.

items.statement: In lab driving tests, people drove just as well soon after THC, the main active part of cannabis, as after a dummy.
items.why: In 80 pooled lab studies, people weaved more in their lane and reacted more slowly than after a dummy.
items.old_statement: Soon after THC, the main active part of cannabis, people did just as well on lab driving tests as after a dummy.

items.statement: Taking benzos such as Xanax or Valium for a long time has been shown to cause dementia.
items.why: Not shown: neither of two studies could rule out that early dementia, which can bring worry and poor sleep, led to the prescriptions. Quebec records linked long use to Alzheimer's, but a Seattle study that tested people found no clear link with the heaviest use.
items.old_statement: Taking benzodiazepines for a long time has been shown to cause dementia.

items.statement: In a lab test, people rated trips on LSD and on psilocybin, the drug in magic mushrooms, as much alike.
items.why: In 28 people, the ratings barely differed. But that's no proof they're the same, and most could tell which drug they'd had.
items.old_statement: In a lab test, people rated LSD and psilocybin trips much alike.

items.statement: In death records from 27 US states, kratom was usually the only drug found when it was named a cause of death.
items.why: Only 7 of 91 had kratom alone; other drugs turned up in the rest, and fentanyl was named as a cause in 51.
items.old_statement: In death records from 27 US states, most deaths where kratom was named as a cause had no other drug found.

items.statement: When doctors wrote up people with health problems after laughing gas, most had numbness or tingling.
items.why: Of 100 people in published reports, 80 had numbness or tingling and 58 had trouble walking. Not all used it for fun: 25 had been given it in surgery.
items.old_statement: In doctors' reports of health problems after laughing gas, most people had numbness or tingling.

items.statement: In safety reports about ecstasy, death was more common when the report also named an antidepressant.
items.why: In US reports, those cases had about 1.6 times the odds of a fatal outcome, and reports naming muscle relaxants or anesthetics had higher odds still. These are voluntary reports, so they can't show cause, and nobody knows how many people took each mix.
items.old_statement: In safety reports about ecstasy, cases that also named an antidepressant more often ended in death.

items.statement: In studies of twins, the twin who used cannabis as a teen, mostly lightly, lost clearly more IQ than the other twin.
items.why: No clear extra loss, though these studies could miss a small one. One study found about 6 points lost after years of dependence.
items.old_statement: In twin studies of mostly light teen use, the twin who used cannabis lost clearly more IQ than the other.

items.statement: In a lab study, caffeine made people with a caffeine habit more alert than people who rarely have it.
items.why: Caffeine only brought them up to the alertness of people who rarely have it. One study; people chose their own habits.
items.old_statement: In a lab study, caffeine made people who have it often more alert than people who rarely have it.

items.statement: In a lab study, after caffeine, people who have it often were more alert than people who rarely have it.
items.why: Caffeine only brought them up to the alertness of people who rarely have it. One study; people chose their own habits.
items.old_statement: In a lab study, caffeine made people who have it often more alert than people who rarely have it.

items.statement: In 2001 Portugal made it no longer a crime to have any drug for your own use. After that, drug use fell.
items.why: It rose slightly, from about 8 to 12 in 100 adults ever trying one. Treatment grew too, so the law's effect is unclear.
items.old_statement: After Portugal stopped treating having any drug for your own use as a crime in 2001, drug use fell.

items.statement: After meeting a 'being' on DMT, fewer people call themselves atheists. The same happens after drug-free 'God' encounters.
items.why: Among people who'd had such meetings, 28 in 100 recalled being atheists before a DMT encounter and 10 in 100 said they were now, and the share fell without drugs too. But they were recalling old beliefs years later.
items.old_statement: Fewer people call themselves atheists after a DMT 'being' encounter, and after drug-free 'God' encounters too.

items.statement: In lab tests, men who were told their drink had vodka in it drank more, whatever was really in the glass.
items.why: They drank about twice as much in 15 minutes, while real vodka made no clear difference to how much they drank. These were lab tests from the 1970s and 1980s, with low blood alcohol.
items.old_statement: In lab tests, men told their drink had vodka drank more, whatever was really in it.

items.statement: In studies, people who had been off cocaine for more than about 5 months still scored clearly lower on memory tests.
items.why: Their scores were close to the comparison groups. But these were other people, not the same people tested again.
items.old_statement: In 5 studies, people who had stopped cocaine for more than about 5 months still scored clearly lower on memory tests.

items.statement: Regular cannabis use can come with bouts of severe vomiting. In most reported cases, it ended when people stopped using.
items.why: Of 64 people whose stopping was recorded, 62 got completely better. Nobody knows how common it is.
items.old_statement: Regular cannabis use can come with bouts of severe vomiting that ended when people stopped, in most reported cases.

items.statement: In one study, people a year or more off heavy cannabis use did as well on tests as people who hadn't used.
items.why: They scored no differently on any test, and a big review found smaller gaps in studies that asked people to stop for over 3 days. But few studies have followed people that long, and researchers disagree.
items.old_statement: In one study, people off heavy cannabis use for a year or more scored like people who hadn't used.

items.statement: Caffeine kept people awake longer in the night, yet in five studies people did not say they had been awake more.
items.why: Across 24 studies, caffeine made falling asleep slower and time awake longer; in five, people did not report more time awake.
items.old_statement: Caffeine added time awake in the night, yet in five studies people did not report more time awake.

items.statement: In studies, caffeine added time awake in the night. Yet in five of them, people did not report being awake more.
items.why: Across 24 studies, caffeine made falling asleep slower and time awake longer; in five, people did not report more time awake.
items.old_statement: Caffeine added time awake in the night, yet in five studies people did not report more time awake.

items.statement: Most volunteers in one lab study ranked a single session on psilocybin, the magic-mushroom drug, among their 5 most meaningful experiences.
items.why: Two months later, 67 in 100 did. But everyone in that study already took part in religious or spiritual activities, which may have made them see it as more spiritual.
items.old_statement: Most volunteers in one lab study ranked a single psilocybin session among their 5 most meaningful experiences.

items.statement: Given LSD or psilocybin without being told which, most people can't tell which one it was.
items.why: By the 28-person study's own figures, people named the right drug in most sessions, though the trips were rated alike.
items.old_statement: Most people can't tell LSD from psilocybin if not told which they got.

items.statement: In a US survey, people who used LSD or mushrooms had more mental health problems, even after counting their other differences.
items.why: Before counting, problems were about 2 to 3 times as common; after counting other drugs, risk-taking and stressful events, none of 20 was higher.
items.old_statement: In a US survey, people who used LSD or mushrooms still had more mental health problems once other differences were counted.

items.statement: In a US survey, people who used LSD or mushrooms had more mental health problems than otherwise similar people who had not.
items.why: Before counting, problems were about 2 to 3 times as common; after counting other drugs, risk-taking and stressful events, none of 20 was higher.
items.old_statement: In a US survey, people who used LSD or mushrooms still had more mental health problems once other differences were counted.

items.statement: In lab studies, about 1 in 11 volunteers reported a short flashback after LSD or psilocybin, the drug in magic mushrooms.
items.why: Of 142 healthy lab volunteers, 13 said they had a flashback, usually a few seconds of changed seeing.
items.old_statement: In lab studies, about 1 in 11 volunteers reported a short flashback after LSD or psilocybin.

items.statement: Scans show serotonin changes in people who used ecstasy, and these changes are known to be permanent.
items.why: Nobody knows: three studies found more of the scan marker in people who had stopped longer ago, two found no link with time, and no one has been scanned while using and again years later.
items.old_statement: The serotonin changes seen on scans of people who used ecstasy are known to be permanent.

items.statement: Cannabis is linked to car crashes just as strongly once studies take drivers' drinking into account.
items.why: It shrinks: studies that allowed for alcohol found about 1.1 to 1.2 times the odds of a crash, against 1.7 to 1.8 in studies that didn't. These compare crashed drivers with others, so they can't show one driver's chance of crashing.
items.old_statement: The link between cannabis and car crashes stays just as strong when studies allow for drinking.
